results.claim: Exact certificate characterization: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor exactly when it has six pairwise-disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4 such that A and B are anticomplete and every other pair of sets has an edge between it. Consequently detection is in NP and has an O(7^n n²) exact algorithm.
results.proof_sketch: An induced-minor model gives these sets as the inverse images of the six target vertices under contractions. The absent target edge forces A and B to be anticomplete, since edge deletion is unavailable. Conversely, contract each connected set; all fourteen required edges appear and the A-B edge does not. For the algorithm, assign every vertex one of seven labels: unused or one of the six branch sets. For each assignment, test nonemptiness, connectivity, the forbidden A-B adjacency, and the fourteen required adjacencies. The labels themselves are a polynomial-size NP certificate.

results.claim: Let q be the number of nonedges of G. Detection is fixed-parameter tractable in q, in time O(7^(2q+3)n²), and undecided instances have at most 2q+3 vertices. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when q=O(log n).
results.proof_sketch: If q=0, G is complete and cannot contain two anticomplete nonempty branch sets. If q>0 and G has at least four universal vertices, the endpoints of any nonedge together with four universal vertices induce K6 minus that edge. Otherwise there are at most three universal vertices. Every remaining vertex is an endpoint of a nonedge, so there are at most 2q such vertices and n≤2q+3. Apply the seven-label algorithm from the first claim. This also gives a kernel: output a fixed yes/no instance in the two decided cases and retain G otherwise.

results.claim: On chordal graphs, K6 minus an edge is an induced minor if and only if it is already an induced subgraph. Thus chordal inputs can be decided in O(n^6) time by enumerating six vertices. The same argument works for Kt minus an edge for every fixed t≥3.
results.proof_sketch: Take a branch model and restrict G to its six branch sets. Each Ci supplies an A-B path whose internal vertices lie in Ci, so every separator disjoint from A∪B has size at least four. Choose an inclusion-minimal A-B separator S. Minimality makes each s∈S adjacent into both components DA and DB containing A and B. If two vertices of S were nonadjacent, shortest paths between them through DA and DB would form an induced cycle of length at least four; hence S is a clique. Each full component D contains a vertex complete to S: choose v∈D maximizing |N(v)∩S|. If s∈S misses v, take a shortest path v=p0,…,pk in D to a neighbor pk of s. For every t∈N(v)∩S, applying chordality to the cycle through t,p0,…,pk,s (using the last neighbor of t on the path) forces tpk to be an edge. Then pk has strictly more neighbors in S than v, a contradiction. Select S-complete vertices x∈DA and y∈DB and four vertices of S. Since x and y lie in different components, these six vertices induce precisely K6 minus xy.

results.claim: There is an explicit polynomial-time classification on complete multipartite graphs. Let the part sizes be n1,…,nr. For every i with ni≥2, reserve two vertices of part i and put mi=ni−2 and mj=nj for j≠i. Accept exactly when, for some s∈{0,…,4} and some s distinct indices J⊆{1,…,r}\{i}, subtracting one from each mj with j∈J leaves counts whose complete multipartite graph has a matching of size at least 4−s. If the residual total is M and its largest part has size L, this matching size is min(⌊M/2⌋,M−L).
results.proof_sketch: The two anticomplete exceptional branch sets must lie in one part: fixing a vertex in either set forces every vertex of the other set, and then of both sets, into that same part. Since a part is independent and each branch set is connected, both are singletons. A core branch touching them is either a singleton in another part or spans at least two parts. Any spanning branch can be shrunk to one cross-part edge; such an edge is adjacent to every other spanning branch and to every outside-part singleton. Singleton core branches must occupy distinct outside parts. Thus choose their part set J, and the remaining core branches are exactly disjoint cross-part edges, namely a matching. The displayed matching formula follows by pairing vertices from different parts: at most ⌊M/2⌋ edges are possible, and every edge uses a vertex outside a largest part, giving M−L; greedily pairing different largest remaining parts attains the minimum. Enumerating i,s,J costs O(r^5), after finding the parts as complement components.

results.claim: Given a tree decomposition of width w, detection is decidable in n·2^{O(w log w)} time; hence it is polynomial-time solvable on every fixed-width class supplied with such decompositions.
results.proof_sketch: Use a nice tree decomposition. A state assigns each bag vertex one of the six branch labels or unused; records, for every label, the partition of its bag vertices into connected components already built; records whether that label is unseen, active, or completed; and stores fourteen bits for required inter-branch adjacencies. Processing an edge merges same-label components, sets the appropriate adjacency bit, or rejects an A-B edge. When the last bag vertex of a component is forgotten, separator locality implies that component cannot connect later, so it may disappear only as the unique component of its label, after which that label is closed. Join nodes combine partitions and adjacency bits. At the root require six nonempty connected labels and all fourteen bits. There are at most 7^(w+1)·Bell(w+1) times a constant number of states, which is 2^{O(w log w)}.

results.claim: A model cannot in general be normalized so that either endpoint of the missing edge has a singleton branch set. A 12-vertex counterexample consists of anticomplete paths A=a1a2a3a4 and B=b1b2b3b4, a clique C={c1,c2,c3,c4}, and exactly the additional edges aici and bici for i=1,…,4.
results.proof_sketch: The two paths and the four singleton sets {ci} form a valid model. Suppose instead that an exceptional branch is {x}. Its four core neighbors require four distinct neighbors of x. Path vertices have degree at most three, so x=ci. The other exceptional branch Y is a connected interval in one component of A−ai or B−bi. Its four core neighbors require |N(Y)\Y|≥4. Up to swapping A,B and reversing indices, take x=c1 or c2. For c2, every allowable interval has at most three external neighbors. For c1, the only intervals with four external neighbors are {a2,a3} and {a2,a3,a4}. Their respective external neighborhoods are {a1,a4,c2,c3} and {a1,c2,c3,c4}. Four disjoint core branches must therefore use all four boundary vertices, including a1. But a1 is isolated after deleting x and Y, so its core branch is the singleton {a1}, anticomplete to the other three core branches—a contradiction. Symmetry handles all remaining cases.

final_writeup:
The unrestricted P-versus-NP-complete classification is not resolved here. The main positive structural result is that contractions give no additional power on chordal inputs: detection reduces to finding the six-vertex induced subgraph, yielding an elementary polynomial algorithm. Complete multipartite graphs admit a separate exact count-and-matching criterion, while arbitrary dense graphs have an FPT kernel in the number of missing edges. A standard connectivity dynamic program also handles supplied bounded-width decompositions.

The principal remaining obstacle is genuine: the two anticomplete exceptional branch sets can both require multiple vertices. The explicit 12-vertex construction rules out algorithms that merely enumerate a nonadjacent vertex pair and search for four remaining branches. Thus the partial results isolate tractable regimes without assuming the normalization that fails in general.
